Title: BRICS payments system now connects to 185 countries

Summary: 
The BRICS-linked Cross-Border Interbank Payments System (CIPS), managed by China’s central bank, now operates in 185 countries, enabling international payments in Chinese yuan without reliance on the U.S. dollar. According to the New Development Bank (NDB), CIPS has facilitated 52 trillion yuan in settlements this year—58% of China’s total cross-border transactions—surpassing the dollar in certain metrics. Trade between China and Russia is settled in local currencies, covering 95% of their trade volume for three consecutive years. Developing economies in Africa, Asia, and Eastern Europe increasingly use CIPS, particularly for Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) loan repayments, while Europe, North America, and Australia have not joined. China launched a yuan-pegged stablecoin, AxCNH, at the 10th BRI Summit, initially deployed in Kazakhstan, to support infrastructure-related cross-border settlements. The NDB plans to issue rupee-denominated bonds by 2026, targeting $300 million to $500 million in 3- to 5-year tranches, as part of a broader strategy to reduce dollar dependence. At the UN General Assembly on September 27, BRICS foreign ministers denounced U.S. tariffs as 'proliferation of trade-restrictive actions,' with Brazilian President Lula da Silva calling them 'tariff blackmail.' Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump has escalated rhetoric against BRICS, calling it an 'Anti-American' bloc and pledging 100% tariffs on countries adopting its policies. In July, he stated he would 'never allow a U.S. central bank digital currency' and vowed to protect the dollar’s reserve status. Despite earlier plans, Brazil dropped the idea of a shared BRICS currency but advanced BRICS Pay, a local-currency settlement platform. BRICS expanded in 2024 with the addition of Iran and Indonesia and continues to meet under its multilateral framework, issuing indirect criticism of U.S. military and trade policies during the Brazil summit, reinforcing its goal of establishing independent financial and payment systems outside Western control.

The article notes China’s leadership in high‑quality development—Beidou navigation, the C929 aircraft, green‑low‑carbon exports such as new‑energy vehicles, lithium batteries and solar cells, and its status as the world’s largest industrial‑robot market for 12 consecutive years with 7,000+ advanced‑level and 230+ excellence‑level smart factories. Indonesian research director Arafat Fibriandi highlighted opportunities for Indonesia to adopt Chinese smart‑factory technologies through joint ventures. Chinese tech leaders Lei Jun of Xiaomi and Zhou Hongyi of 360 Group called on BRICS to become a testing ground for AI‑enabled industrialisation. The piece also focuses on Fujian’s role: its digital‑economy added value accounts for 55 % of provincial GDP, 133 “Silk‑Road maritime” routes reach 46 countries, and 20 million overseas Chinese live in 193 countries. In 2024 Fujian’s exports to BRICS reached 358.4 billion RMB, about one‑fifth of total exports, shifting from traditional light‑industry to high‑value‑added products such as new‑energy buses and high‑end equipment. The Xiamen BRICS Innovation Base has launched a science‑innovation incubation park and the “Golden‑Heron” scholarship to train talent in industry and communications.

Key quotes: 
- Alexey Grigiev: '历次工业革命中，有国家、城市兴起，也有国家被迫掉队，我们绝不能重蹈覆辙，第四次工业革命必须包容发展，而非排他分化。'
- Dilma Rousseff: '工业化仍是长期发展的核心支柱，但工业化的理念必须升级。'
- Lei Jun: '金砖国家凭借庞大的产业基础与市场需求，有望成为人工智能赋能新型工业化的试验田和引领者。'
- Zhou Hongyi: '愿意面向金砖国家开放智能体工厂技术，提供从智能体构建到场景落地的全链条赋能。'

Metrics: 34 countries, 55 % digital‑economy added value, 133 maritime routes to 46 countries, 20 million overseas Chinese, 358.4 billion RMB exports to BRICS in 2024.

articles.title: China Challenges U.S. 'Superpower' Status
articles.summary: The article reports that China’s 2025 Victory Day parade in Beijing, attended by 26 state and government leaders from Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America—including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić and Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico—featured 12,000 soldiers and the country’s most modern weapon systems. According to the article, China’s goal is to become the actor that sets the rules in the future world order. Experts quoted in the piece, such as Prof. Eberhard Sandschneider, describe such parades as tools for autocracies to display real or symbolic power, while Soong of MERICS notes that China’s economic rise is reinforcing its international role. The article cites China’s 1.4 billion population and its 2049 modernization target, and states that “modeling suggests China will overtake the U.S. economy in 5 or at most 15 years.” It also outlines China’s Belt and Road Initiative, BRICS, Shanghai Cooperation Organization, and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, noting that recipient countries often bear heavy debt burdens. The piece includes a quote from German PM Friedrich Merz: ‘Those who truly want to understand the challenges should travel not only to China but also to Asian countries.’ The article is analytical, presenting data, expert commentary and direct quotes while maintaining a largely factual tone.

articles.title: Xi Jinping's China: A Defense Strategy (and 4)
articles.summary: China has accelerated its defensive and international cooperation strategy in response to a military and geopolitical encirclement by the United States and its allies, according to a recent article from Acento. The piece argues that China, which became an economic powerhouse without a military superpower, now faces the risk of US military action after failed trade and technology wars. It cites US military agreements with Japan, South Korea, the Philippines, Taiwan, Australia, and other neighboring countries, as well as AUKUS and the QUAD, as attempts to contain China. The article claims China has no military bases abroad except one in Africa and no formal military alliances with Russia, India, Iran, or Pakistan, preferring instead to maintain friendly relations. It highlights China’s emphasis on building land corridors—roads, railways, pipelines—to bypass maritime choke points such as the Strait of Malacca, Suez, Gibraltar, and Panama. The author also notes China’s support for multilateral groups like BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, and its Global Development Initiative aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals. The piece concludes that China’s strategy is to create a vast terrestrial communication network across Eurasia, countering US naval dominance, while also projecting power through displays such as the recent 80‑year‑anniversary parade. The article’s tone is strongly pro‑China, framing US actions as aggressive and portraying China as a peaceful, cooperative partner. Notable quotes include: 'mientras a China le preocupa tener pocos amigos, a EUA le preocupa tener pocos enemigos' and 'Te lo dije, pues, conociendo los peligros a que te enfrentas, ¿cómo vas a permitir que tus dirigentes estén conectados en WhatsApp, Waze o los sistemas de geolocalización de Google?'

articles.title: The BRICS 'Laboratory' and the EU's Strategic Autonomy
articles.summary: The Chinese Communist Party's fourth plenary session is scheduled for October, where the party will deliberate on the outlines of its next five-year plan. The session will bring together over 370 members of the Central Committee, the party's elite. The plan will need to consider the impact of the new 'law' of tariffs imposed by the US, which has made China the target of this new 'law'. The session will take place shortly after the Chinese parade celebrating the end of World War II, where Vladimir Putin will be a guest of honor, and before the APEC summit in Seoul. The plan will need to address the intensification of the US-China trade, technological, and geopolitical war. China's new technological decisions in 2025 will define the roadmap for all areas, from artificial intelligence to quantum computing, biotechnology, and controlled nuclear fusion. The EU, which has committed 'suicide' by engaging in a series of self-destructive actions, will be left out of the decision-making process. The article highlights the EU's dependence on Chinese technology and materials, and its inability to compete with the US. The author notes that the EU's only option is to accept the US's 'offer you can't refuse' and invest in US infrastructure and the military-industrial complex. The article concludes that the EU is a pitiful actor on the world stage, with its strategic autonomy below zero, and is ignored in the US's eternal wars. The author also notes that China is more cunning and has offered the EU a 'green' deal, while the US has imposed a 'tariff law' on the EU. The article ends with a commentary by Yuen Yuen Ang, a professor of economics at Johns Hopkins University, who notes that the EU suffers from a 'deficit of attention' and that the US's policy is based on a 'accumulation of absurd messages'. She also notes that China is shifting from an export-oriented economy to a high-tech and innovation-driven economy, and that the EU should learn from China's 'improvisation-directed' approach.

articles.title: India and China Accelerate Their Rapprochement
articles.summary: India and China have agreed to re-open trade through their Himalayan border crossings and re-establish direct flights, suspended since 2020, in the most significant thaw in relations between the two powers. The agreements were announced yesterday by the Indian Ministry of External Affairs after a two-day visit by Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, who met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. According to the statement, both countries agreed to 'reopen border trade through the three commercial points' and 'resume direct flight connectivity as soon as possible.' They also agreed to facilitate visa issuance for tourists and businesspeople. In the context of the tense border dispute, both parties agreed to create a 'Group of Experts' to explore an accelerated advance in border demarcation, as well as a 'working group' to effectively manage the border and prevent future confrontations. Beijing has also expressed support for India to host the BRICS summit in 2026, while New Delhi will support China for the 2027 edition. This rapprochement, aimed at rebuilding bridges after the deadly border clashes of 2020, comes at a time of maximum commercial tension between India and the US, following the imposition of a 50% tariff on Indian products. 'The Chinese side welcomed the Indian Prime Minister Modi's attendance at the SCO Summit to be held in Tianjin,' concludes the statement. The relations between the two Asian powers were at their lowest point in decades after the June 2020 military clash in the Galwan Valley, in the disputed Himalayan border, in which at least 20 Indian soldiers and four Chinese soldiers were killed. In recent months, and especially in the last few weeks, a rapid thaw has taken place, which began with India's re-establishment of tourist visas in July and culminated this week with Wang's visit to New Delhi and the announcements made.

articles.title: 2025 BRICS New Industrial Revolution Partnership Forum Opens in Xiamen
articles.summary:
The 2025 BRICS New Industrial Revolution Partnership Forum, held in Xiamen for two days, opened with a theme of '释放大金砖合作潜力 实现包容可持续工业化' ("Release the potential of Big BRICS cooperation and achieve inclusive, sustainable industrialization"). The forum, jointly hosted by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the Fujian provincial government, attracted representatives from 34 governments and industry groups, including BRICS members Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa, as well as partner countries Kazakhstan, Cuba, and Nigeria. 

Key metrics: the forum featured 1396 innovation projects across five tracks—artificial intelligence, green industry, low‑altitude equipment, energy electronics, and industrial design—leading to awards of 1 first‑place, 2 second‑place, and 3 third‑place projects. The BRICS Industrial Capability China Center was unveiled, publishing the "2025 BRICS Industrial Cooperation Case Collection". The BRICS New Industrial "金鹭" Excellence Scholarship was launched to support talent exchange and project collaboration among BRICS and Global South countries.

During the opening ceremony, a video showcased the BRICS Innovation Base’s achievements over five years in policy coordination, talent training, and project development. The base, established in 2020 in Xiamen, has signed 107 projects with a total investment exceeding 50.6 billion CNY and hosted more than 40 high‑level international exchanges.

Economic data highlighted that in 2024 Fujian’s trade with BRICS countries reached 358.4 billion CNY, accounting for nearly one‑fifth of the province’s total trade. Exports to BRICS shifted from traditional goods (clothing, footwear, furniture) toward high‑value products such as new‑energy vehicles and advanced equipment. By July 2025, 782 new enterprises had been established in Fujian with BRICS investment, generating 3.34 billion USD in foreign‑direct‑investment contracts and 6.64 billion USD in Chinese investment. Xiamen’s customs data showed that from September 2017 to July 2025, trade with BRICS countries totaled 662.72 billion CNY, with exports of 228 billion CNY and imports of 434.72 billion CNY.

The forum also launched the BRICS Digital Industry Ecological Cooperation Network Xiamen node and released the "New Industrialization International Cooperation Initiative" expansion plan, aiming to standardize cooperation, promote advanced technologies, share green development experience, and strengthen industrial cluster collaboration.

Overall, the event underscored the growing role of BRICS in shaping a new industrial revolution, with Xiamen positioned as a key hub for policy coordination, talent development, and industrial partnership.
